account: Sky Sentinel is an automated turret, a heavy machine gun on a 360-degree mount. Its software, written by Ukrainian engineers, takes radar input and separates drones from birds. It tracks the target and computes the ballistic solution. UNITED24 Media, the outlet of the UNITED24 fundraising platform, reported on 26 May 2025 that one prototype had downed four Shahed drones at the front. Dates and places were withheld for security. UNITED24 said that its $1.5 million campaign for 10 turrets at about $150,000 each was complete. Forbes (David Hambling, 27 May 2025), as relayed by Euromaidan Press on 28 May 2025, repeats the four kills. It gives a pointing precision of 17 micro-radians. Business Insider reported on 2 June 2025 that the commander of a Ukrainian air defense group said that one prototype had downed six Shaheds in six uses. He said that the turret needs human authorization before it fires. The OECD Monitor entry also states that a human authorizes each shot. The Defense Post (3 June 2025) describes the turret as firing on its own. It adds that 10 to 30 units would be needed to protect a city and that production is scaling to dozens a month. UNITED24 reported that it had raised $3.3 million for 22 systems by February 2026. Five systems went to the 636th Separate Anti-Aircraft Machine Gun Battalion in Sumy region in August 2026. On 5 October 2026 the Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat said that AI-aimed turrets had downed Russian jet-powered drones. The Kyiv Independent, which relayed his statement, names no turret model. On 23 October 2026 UNITED24 reported that more than 12 turrets were on duty in Kyiv.

ai_role.statement: The commander interviewed by Business Insider said that once the turret receives radar data, it scans the airspace, identifies and tracks targets and determines the firing point, and that it needs human authorization before it fires. UNITED24 describes the operator as monitoring the system while the turret handles aiming. The kill counts come from the unit and the fundraiser, and no source compares the turret with manually aimed guns.

fields.account: Sky Sentinel is an automated turret, a heavy machine gun on a 360-degree mount. Its software, written by Ukrainian engineers, takes radar input and separates drones from birds. It tracks the target and computes the ballistic solution. UNITED24 Media, the outlet of the UNITED24 fundraising platform, reported on 26 May 2025 that one prototype had downed four Shahed drones at the front. Dates and places were withheld for security. UNITED24 said that its $1.5 million campaign for 10 turrets at about $150,000 each was complete. Forbes (David Hambling, 27 May 2025), as relayed by Euromaidan Press on 28 May 2025, repeats the four kills. It gives a pointing precision of 17 micro-radians. Business Insider reported on 2 June 2025 that the commander of a Ukrainian air defense group said that one prototype had downed six Shaheds in six uses. He said that the turret needs human authorization before it fires. The OECD Monitor entry also states that a human authorizes each shot. The Defense Post (3 June 2025) describes the turret as firing on its own. It adds that 10 to 30 units would be needed to protect a city and that production is scaling to dozens a month. UNITED24 reported that it had raised $3.3 million for 22 systems by February 2026. Five systems went to the 636th Separate Anti-Aircraft Machine Gun Battalion in Sumy region in August 2026. On 5 October 2026 the Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat said that AI-aimed turrets had downed Russian jet-powered drones. The Kyiv Independent, which relayed his statement, names no turret model. On 23 October 2026 UNITED24 reported that more than 12 turrets were on duty in Kyiv.
fields.summary: A prototype of Sky Sentinel, a Ukrainian AI-aimed machine-gun turret, downed six Shaheds in six uses, a unit commander said; more than 12 turrets were on duty in Kyiv by October 2026.
